SpaceX proves Falcon Heavy is indeed a real rocket with a test firing - video link in comments

What's cool about the Falcon Heavy is that for the first phase of launch, the strap-on rockets send their fuel to the core rocket. When the strap-ons run dry and jettison, the core rocket has nearly all of its fuel remaining. This greatly improves the efficiency and therefore can handle heavier payloads.

I'm not too pessimistic about the use of such a large number of engines. Unlike other rockets, SpaceX can use strap-ons that have already survived a complete flight, since the rockets are reusable. And their engines are restartable during flight, so some mishaps are recoverable. It's more like trying to fly 10 brand-new jetliners at once than the ghastly Soviet N1 rocket.
